task.description:
Design a fix for the ISS-0113/ISS-0423-disclosed remaining hazard that ISS-0480 caught recurring in the wild: `Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1`'s unconditional `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` call (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:222) is a GLOBAL per-repo setting, so any one of the 44 still-unconverted call sites running mid-suite forcibly checks in EVERY other concurrently-running async test's connection -- including tests that never call provisioned_tenant!/1 themselves and have no way to defend against it. Read this run's ISSUE-FIXER diagnosis (handoffs/WF03-ISS0480-20260905/step-0.5-1-issue-fixer-diagnose.json result.summary) in full first -- it traces the mechanism through Ecto's own sandbox.ex source (mode/2's documented 'checks in connections being used in any other test running concurrently' behaviour) and captured three live, real occurrences across two full-suite runs, each against a different victim test. This is not a fresh investigation; treat the mechanism as established fact.

This is NOT a new root cause -- it is ISS-0113/ISS-0423's own explicitly disclosed remaining scope (44 of 46 TenantFixture call sites unconverted) actually manifesting. Read docs/issues/ISS-0113.yaml's full resolution_note and docs/issues/ISS-0423.yaml's full resolution_note before designing -- both already contain load-bearing prior art you must not silently re-attempt:
  - ISS-0113's FIRST attempted fix (an opts[:restore_sandbox] opt-in doing Sandbox.mode(:manual) + a fresh checkout after provisioning) was tried for real, passed its own design gate, then FAILED at implementation (26/38) -- traced to a 4th Sandbox.mode/2 mechanism: Ecto's Sandbox.mode/2 checks in ALL pool connections whenever the requested mode differs from the pool's CURRENT one, so a second mid-test mode flip (the restore step itself) discards the connection provisioning had just populated. Do not propose a per-call restore-to-:manual step without addressing this exact failure mode head-on.
  - The mechanism that DID work for the 2 already-converted files (secrets_test.exs, webhooks_test.exs) is: no restore at all, relying on the pre-existing unconditional :auto call being 'ALREADY SUFFICIENT... PROVIDED the call site is independently verified' against three (now four, per ISS-0423's own resolution note) named failure mechanisms (self-checkout, concurrent multi-process DB access, second provisioning call, and this run's own newly-confirmed global-blast-radius-on-OTHER-files mechanism). That per-call-site verification approach is exactly what leaves 44 sites (and therefore every OTHER async: true test in the suite, including files with NO TenantFixture involvement at all, like ISS-0480's own two victims) permanently exposed until every site is converted or defended -- which is why ISS-0480 recurred.

YOUR DESIGN MUST DECIDE, and justify the choice with reasoning grounded in the diagnosis (not merely restate the options): 
(a) NARROW: continue the per-call-site conversion tranche approach (verify + flip async:false->true one file at a time against the four named mechanisms) for some or all of the remaining 44 TenantFixture call sites. This does NOT close the hazard for the two ISS-0480 victim files themselves (they already ARE async: true and call NO fixture) -- it only reduces how often the global mode-flip fires, proportional to how many of the 44 you convert. State plainly whether a partial narrow conversion actually protects RowApprovalTest/PackUpdateMigrationTest, or whether ONLY converting all 44 (or another structural change) removes their exposure. 
(b) STRUCTURAL: remove the global-blast-radius hazard at its source, so files with NO TenantFixture involvement (like ISS-0480's own two victims) stop being exposed regardless of how many of the 44 remaining call sites are converted or not. Concrete directions worth evaluating (not prescriptive -- you decide, but show your reasoning against each): a separate, dedicated Ecto.Repo/connection pool for TenantFixture-provisioned tenant schemas so its Sandbox.mode/2 flips never touch Letflow.Repo's pool that ordinary DataCase tests use; or moving provisioned_tenant!/1's schema provisioning off the sandboxed Repo pool entirely (e.g. a raw, non-sandboxed connection dedicated to migration replay, never touching Sandbox.mode/2 on the shared pool at all); or something else you identify as removing the mode/2 call's global reach. Check each candidate against decision 0009-test-parallel-pool-sizing.md's DBConnection budget arithmetic (a second pool/connection changes peak concurrent connection demand) and against Letflow.SandboxPool's own existing moduledoc (test/support -- there is already a quota-bounded, owner-monitored pool abstraction in this codebase built for exactly this shape; evaluate whether it's reusable here or whether TenantFixture's needs are different enough to warrant its own mechanism).

Whichever direction you choose, or if you choose a hybrid, your design's normative section must be unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without further judgement calls, per this project's weak-model-tolerance standard. State explicitly: what changes, what does NOT change (public API of provisioned_tenant!/1, error taxonomy, any existing call site's return shape), and what verification ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-DESIGNER must run to prove the fix actually closes ISS-0480's specific exposure (RowApprovalTest and PackUpdateMigrationTest must stop being vulnerable to ANY concurrently-running TenantFixture-using test, not merely stop failing in one lucky run -- a fail-then-pass regression test per WF-03 Step 4 must be able to demonstrate this, so your design should suggest how such a test could deterministically trigger the hazard pre-fix, e.g. by forcing a concurrent provisioned_tenant!/1 call while a DataCase-only test holds an in-flight transaction, mirroring ISS-0110's own targeted-reproduction technique of simulating the race directly rather than relying on suite-wide timing luck).

Do not touch supervision-tree files. Do not write implementation code -- design artefact only, in lib/letflow/design/, per this project's design/implementation split.
acceptance_criteria: Design artefact written to lib/letflow/design/ (a new file, or a new section appended to lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md if you judge it the same design lineage -- your call, state which and why)

Explicitly addresses whether a narrow per-call-site conversion tranche can ever fully protect a file with zero TenantFixture involvement (like ISS-0480's two victims), or whether only a structural fix does -- this determines whether ISS-0480 can be marked resolved by this fix or only instrumented
Does not re-propose the exact restore_sandbox mechanism ISS-0113 already tried and reverted, without explaining what is different this time if some variant of it is chosen
States precisely what changes and what does not (public API, error taxonomy, existing call sites' behavior)
Reconciles against decision 0009-test-parallel-pool-sizing.md's DBConnection budget arithmetic if the design adds any connection/pool

Describes a concrete, deterministic mechanism TEST-DESIGNER can use to construct a fail-then-pass regression test for ISS-0480's specific exposure (a forced concurrent TenantFixture call racing a plain DataCase test), not merely 'run the suite many times and hope it reproduces'
No implementation code in the design artefact (design signatures/@specs/data-flow only)
